messages.subject: .rhtml files execution
parts:
Hi Everyone,
I am new to use java script with RApache, I have
installed brew package. Goal is that my web user interface should
produce a plot with the dataset uploaded by the user.

For now I am using known dataset, so I know about the column headers
and I wrote R code according to that, i am little confused on how to
set for a different dataset. Lets say user is uploading a totally
different dataset with different column headers and user interface
should ask for the columns and then produce the plot with R code.

And next thing is about calling .rhtml ( r code files ) in to the
javascript. Can any one explain taking my sample app code given below:

Any one plzz guide me to separate R code in to .rhtml file and then hw
to execute that .rhtml file from the form after uploading the dataset.

<html>
<body>
<form enctype="multipart/form-data" method="POST" action="http://
localhost/brew/test99.html">
<input type="file" name="FirstFile">
<input type="submit" name="Upload">
</form>

<pre>
<code>
<%
g <- read.csv(FILES$FirstFile$tmp_name, header=T)
print(head(g));
setwd('/var/www')
print(getwd());
jpeg('bglot.jpg');


library(car)
library(MASS)
scatterplot(Qvalue ~ PosSamples | Cancer, data=g, xlab="Positive
Samples", ylab="Qvalue", main="Enhanced Scatter Plot", labels=g
$Genes);

dev.off();
%>
</pre>
</code>
<p>
Scatter plot<br>
<iframe src="http://localhost/bglot.jpg" width="500" height="500">
click here</iframe>
</p>


</body>
</html>

messages.author: 42eed4e1caba0ad0
messages.subject: Re: .rhtml files execution
parts:
OK, this one doesn't satisfy "one question per question" rule, but
anyway... the answer to both questions is AJAX. Just navigate your
browser to W3Schools and read the tutorial, it's quite
straightforward... http://www.w3schools.com/ajax/default.asp

I don't prefer the mashup of HTML and R, since it's too cumbersome for
bookkeeping, so use separate files for R scripts. Jeroen mentioned
something about IE incompatibility with .rhtml files, just search the
mailing list. I really don't have a bloody idea what's happening
within IE when it encounters a .rhtml file. However, you can use
"<FilesMatch>" directive and set some kind of prefix to your R scripts
(like Jeroen did in ggplot webapp, just watch the NET panel in Firebug
upon form submission), then match the scripts with regular expression.
By doing such, you won't mess up the plot file retrieval. If you set
brew::brew to operate on all files in a directory, you're probably not
going to see the desired result, since you practically tell Apache to
use R to process the png file. You don't want that, right?

The main idea is that you should asynchronously call R script (that's
what's AJAX is all about), and load desired content. You can use JSON
to serialise the data (e.g. table data and png file location), there's
RJSONIO package available on CRAN: www.omegahat.org/RJSONIO/

Just don't, I repeat DON'T do the layout stuff with R, use JS instead.
You can set data.frame, working directory and plot path in a list,
then wrap it inside toJSON, something like this:

require(RJSONIO)
g <- read.csv(FILES$FirstFile$tmp_name, header=T)
g_head <- head(g)
setwd("/var/www")
wd <- getwd()
plot_file <- "bglot.jpg"
fpath <- file.path(wd, plot_file)

res <- list(file_preview = g_head, working_directory = wd, plot =
plot_file)

png(fpath)
# do the plotting stuff...
dev.off()

toJSON(res)

# you should wrap this up in several functions, FWIW

Once you return JSON from AJAX call, you can massage the data with
JavaScript. It can be a bit labour-intensive, but you shouldn't do
that within R, use JS to render the stuff on the client side, and
leave computations for the server side (R scripts).

Oh, and try using some JS library to make your life easier (jQuery or
ExtJS), but first, get a firm grasp on JS "per se"!

In that case, you don't need brew, you can easily use sys.source.
Anyway, try naming your R scripts systematically (and leave the
extension, put in the prefix):

rscript-one
rscript-two

Here's an example config file (use .htaccess, not the global conf)

<FilesMatch "^rscript-.[a-z]+$">
SetHandler r-script
RHandler base::sys.source
</FilesMatch>

REvalOnStartup "library(RJSONIO)"

ROutputErrors

Good luck, have fun!
Alex

Oh, and you can also use AJAX to populate select boxes or whatever
with column names. Avoid using "headers" when you talk about R and web-
dev, or be precise. Headers could refer to HTTP headers.
